answer: Rotating Marble Assignment. Each epoch, a public verifiable-random beacon assigns agents to task groups; membership is revealed only after the epoch seed is fixed, so attackers cannot precompute which clones land together. A vine of corroborating peers must independently confirm each agent's work within its assigned group. To swamp a group, an attacker must control many identities across unpredictable groupings, paying full compute and latency per clone every epoch with no guarantee of collusion. The harbor of honest workers stays unflooded because placement is random and unpredictable.
